stem:
Seema stirs a spoon of sugar into a glass of water. Soon no sugar grains can be seen, yet the water tastes sweet throughout the glass.

Which claim best explains this?

options.text: The sugar particles spread into the spaces between the water particles, so sugar is present throughout the water.
The sugar particles gather only at the top of the water, and only that top layer tastes sweet.
The sugar vanishes completely, and only a sweet taste remains with no sugar particles left.
Each water particle takes a sugar particle inside itself, which makes that water particle sweet.

teacher.key_rationale: Dissolved sugar particles spread among water particles, so the sweet taste is present throughout even when grains are no longer visible.
